assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
only public signals are available; platform-internal labels (IP, device, login graph) are not accessible
the unit of analysis is a visible reaction (a wave of engagement), not the legal identity of any single named account
a labeled CIB benchmark can be assembled from published corpora for calibration and FPR/TPR measurement
exclusions: per-account legal attribution to a named operator (delegated to legal/forensic process)
platform-side enforcement, suspension, or takedown mechanics
access to platform-internal telemetry or confirmed ground-truth labels
content veracity / fact-checking of the messages themselves (a separate task from authenticity of the reaction)
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for inauthentic-reaction detection work units, informed by the social-bot and CIB literature; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Ferrara, Varol, Davis, Menczer & Flammini 2016 'The Rise of Social Bots' (Comm. ACM 59:7); Davis, Varol, Ferrara, Flammini & Menczer 2016 'BotOrNot/Botometer' (WWW); Ratkiewicz et al. 2011 'Detecting and Tracking Political Abuse in Social Media' / Truthy (ICWSM); Cresci, Di Pietro, Petrocchi, Spognardi & Tesconi 2017 'The Paradigm-Shift of Social Spambots' (WWW); Meta Adversarial Threat / Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior reports & Graphika network analyses; Platt 1999 'Probabilistic Outputs for Support Vector Machines'; Zadrozny & Elkan 2002 isotonic calibration; Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005 calibration comparison

competency_questions.question: Why is the output a calibrated probability with provenance rather than a boolean bot/human verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROBLEM_FRAMING and OUTPUT_CONTRACT establish probability+provenance and the no-boolean invariant grounded in the absence of public ground truth

competency_questions.question: Which confirming signals are private/unavailable from public data, and how is that gap recorded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NO_GROUND_TRUTH enumerates the private confirming signals; SIGNAL_INVENTORY logs what is proxied

competency_questions.question: What public signals are collected, with what provenance, and how is each estimate traced back to them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_INVENTORY catalogs signals with provenance; EXPLANATION_PROVENANCE traces estimates back

competency_questions.question: How are inauthentic account-level and textual features (age, avatar, copypasta) extracted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_FEATURES and TEMPLATED_TEXT extract account-level and near-duplicate text signals

competency_questions.question: How is temporal coordination (synchronized bursts, lockstep timing) detected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COORDINATION_SIGNALS detects synchronized timing and co-action over defined windows

competency_questions.question: How is inauthentic network structure (sybil rings, dense reciprocal clusters) detected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NETWORK_STRUCTURE mines reciprocal clusters and sybil rings from the interaction graph

competency_questions.question: How is engagement disproportion (views vs comments vs shares) used as a signal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENGAGEMENT_MISMATCH scores cross-channel ratio deviation against matched baselines

competency_questions.question: How are the signal families fused into one inauthenticity score while staying decomposable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FEATURE_FUSION weights families into a decomposable score traceable to logged signals

competency_questions.question: How is the fused score turned into a calibrated probability and propagated to downstream hype metrics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CALIBRATION maps the score to a calibrated probability; CONFIDENCE_PROPAGATION discounts downstream hype

competency_questions.question: How is the probability calibrated (Platt/isotonic) and how is uncertainty quantified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CALIBRATION fits Platt/isotonic and reports FPR/TPR; UNCERTAINTY_QUANT attaches an interval

competency_questions.question: What labeled benchmark measures FPR/TPR and how is its staleness handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VALIDATION_SET curates versioned labeled CIB benchmarks with documented provenance

competency_questions.question: How is detector decay under adversarial adaptation tracked and corrected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADVERSARIAL_ADAPTATION tracks per-signal decay and schedules re-fitting against the benchmark

competency_questions.question: How is the asymmetric cost of false positives encoded in the decision policy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FALSE_POSITIVE_COST encodes explicit asymmetric FP/FN costs feeding an FP-averse policy

competency_questions.question: What provenance, human-review routing, and output contract make each estimate auditable, accountable, and free of a boolean verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HUMAN_REVIEW_THRESHOLD routes by probability/uncertainty; EXPLANATION_PROVENANCE attaches an evidence trail; OUTPUT_CONTRACT enforces probability+provenance with no boolean field

glossary.definition: organized use of multiple accounts to deceive about who is behind a reaction, the unit of analysis in Meta/Graphika takedowns
an automated or semi-automated account that mimics human activity, per Ferrara 2016
fabricated grassroots appearance manufactured by a hidden coordinated source, per Ratkiewicz 2011 Truthy
a cluster of accounts controlled by one operator that mutually reinforce to fake reach
identical or near-identical text reposted across many accounts as a coordination tell
mapping a model score to a probability whose value matches empirical frequency, via Platt 1999 or isotonic regression
a plot of predicted probability vs observed frequency used to assess calibration
a real, authentic user or community wrongly estimated as inauthentic
the logged trail of which signals, weights, examples and model versions produced an estimate

nodes.definition: Frame the task as estimating a calibrated probability P(inauthentic | public signals) for a visible reaction (a wave of comments/likes/shares), never emitting a clean boolean 'bot'/'human' verdict, because public data carries no platform-internal ground truth (IP, device, login graph) that a verdict would require.

base.update_signal: product asks for a hard label, or platform-internal signals become available

included: scope = visible reaction, not a single account's identity
provenance requirement attached to every estimate
excluded: asserting a named account IS a bot

pros.claim: A probability + provenance is defensible and survives appeal; a boolean verdict on public-only signals is not
pros.example: Meta/Graphika CIB reports describe 'coordinated behavior', not per-account guilt verdicts

cons.claim: Probabilities are harder for downstream consumers to act on than a clean yes/no
cons.example: a dashboard wants a single bot flag, not a 0.63

failure_modes: product pressure collapses the probability into a hard threshold and loses calibration
framing as account-level guilt invites defamation risk
acceptance_tests: output schema is a probability in [0,1] plus a provenance object; no boolean verdict field exists
revisit_triggers: a consumer requests a boolean label
scope creeps from reaction-level to account-identity-level

nodes.definition: Encode the core epistemic limit: public signals lack the platform-internal labels (account-creation IP, device fingerprint, phone verification, login co-location, suspension history) that alone could confirm inauthenticity, so any output is an estimate under uncertainty, not a measurement.

base.update_signal: platform grants labelled data, or a new public signal proxies an internal label

included: enumerate which confirming signals are private
uncertainty is irreducible from public data alone
excluded: claiming access to internal platform telemetry
legal attribution to a named operator

pros.claim: Stating the ground-truth gap up front prevents over-claiming and sets honest confidence bounds
pros.example: Ferrara 2016 notes bot detection has no clean public oracle

cons.claim: Acknowledged uncertainty can be weaponized to dismiss real, well-evidenced CIB findings
cons.example: 'you can't prove it' used to wave away a synchronized campaign

failure_modes: treating a strong public proxy as if it were confirmed ground truth
silent assumption that absence of a signal means authenticity
acceptance_tests: every estimate documents which confirming signals were unavailable and were therefore proxied
revisit_triggers: a public signal is found to reliably proxy an internal label
platform partnership supplies partial labels

nodes.definition: Maintain the catalog of observable public signals (account metadata, post text, timing series, engagement counts, follower graph) with, for each, its collection method, freshness, and reliability, so every downstream feature is traceable to a logged, time-stamped source.

base.update_signal: a platform API deprecates a field or rate-limits a signal source

pros.claim: A provenance-first inventory means every probability can be traced back to logged raw signals for audit and appeal
pros.example: Botometer documents exactly which public features it ingests

cons.claim: Public APIs change without notice, silently degrading signals the catalog assumes are present
cons.example: Twitter/X API tier changes removed free timeline access

failure_modes: a deprecated API field feeds stale or empty features unnoticed
sampling bias from rate-limited collection skews the signal set
acceptance_tests: every signal in use has a recorded collection method, timestamp, and reliability rating
revisit_triggers: an API field is deprecated or rate-limited
a new public signal source is added to the catalog

nodes.definition: Extract per-account features that historically separate inauthentic from organic accounts: account age, follower/following ratio anomalies, default/AI-generated avatars, missing bio, high posting volume, and screen-name entropy (random suffixes), per Botometer's account-feature family.

base.update_signal: a new account-creation cohort or avatar-generation technique shifts feature distributions

included: age / follower-following ratio / avatar / bio / name-entropy features

pros.claim: Account features are cheap, fast, and the most studied bot signal family since Davis 2016 Botometer
pros.example: a 3-day-old account following 5000 with 0 followers and a default egg avatar

cons.claim: Account features alone yield high false positives on legitimate new users, brands, and low-effort real people
cons.example: a new real user with a default avatar and no bio looks bot-like

failure_modes: over-weighting age penalizes legitimate new users
avatar heuristics break as default avatars and GAN faces evolve
acceptance_tests: account features are computed for each account with documented anomaly thresholds, not hard cutoffs
revisit_triggers: follower/following norms shift on the platform
a feature's discriminative power decays in validation

nodes.definition: Detect near-duplicate / templated text across the reaction: copypasta, slot-filled templates, and high textual similarity clusters, using shingling/MinHash and edit-distance, a hallmark of spambot and astroturf content per Ratkiewicz 2011 (Truthy) and Cresci 2017.

base.update_signal: template-evasion (spinning/paraphrase/LLM rewriting) raises text diversity

pros.claim: Near-duplicate clustering is a strong, interpretable astroturf signal and was central to Truthy's meme-injection detection
pros.example: 50 replies sharing the same 12-word template with only the @handle swapped

cons.claim: LLM-paraphrased or 'spun' content defeats exact and near-duplicate matching, inflating false negatives
cons.example: a campaign uses a model to rewrite each post uniquely

failure_modes: paraphrase/spinning evades n-gram similarity
legitimate viral catchphrases trigger false copypasta flags
acceptance_tests: near-duplicate clusters are reported with similarity scores and the matching method recorded
revisit_triggers: paraphrase-based evasion observed in validation
a benign viral phrase causes a false-positive cluster

nodes.definition: Detect coordination in the temporal dimension: synchronized posting bursts, abnormally tight inter-arrival times, lockstep activity windows, and co-action (same accounts acting together repeatedly), the defining property of Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior in Meta/Graphika reports.

base.update_signal: coordination definition or burst-window parameters change, or schedulers add jitter

pros.claim: Synchronized timing is the most defensible CIB signal because organic crowds do not act in millisecond lockstep
pros.example: 200 accounts all post within a 90-second window on a 3am local time

cons.claim: Real coordinated-but-authentic activity (fandoms, activism, breaking news) also produces synchronized bursts
cons.example: K-pop fans organically mass-reply on cue

failure_modes: legitimate organized communities are flagged as inauthentic coordination
injected timing jitter defeats tight-window detectors
acceptance_tests: coordination is reported as a co-activity score over a defined window with the window parameters logged
revisit_triggers: bursts traced to an authentic organized community
schedulers add jitter that defeats the current window

nodes.definition: Analyze the follower/interaction graph for inauthentic structure: dense reciprocal follow clusters, sybil rings, star/hub amplification patterns, and unusually high clustering coefficients among the reacting accounts, drawing on Ratkiewicz 2011 diffusion-network analysis and Graphika cluster maps.

base.update_signal: graph-construction policy or the reciprocity/clustering thresholds change

pros.claim: Network structure exposes amplification machinery that single-account features miss, central to Graphika's CIB takedowns
pros.example: a ring of 80 accounts that mutually follow each other and only amplify one source

cons.claim: Public graph data is partial and sampled, so absent edges can fake or hide a ring
cons.example: API limits hide most of the real follower edges

failure_modes: sampled/partial graph yields spurious or missed clusters
legitimate tight-knit communities resemble sybil rings
acceptance_tests: network structure metrics (reciprocity, clustering, dense-subgraph membership) are computed on the logged subgraph
revisit_triggers: graph sampling coverage drops below a usable threshold
a benign community matches a sybil-ring signature

nodes.definition: Detect implausible ratios among engagement types: views-to-likes, likes-to-comments, comment-to-share, and reach-to-conversation, where bot amplification typically inflates one channel (e.g. likes/views) far out of proportion to the genuine-discussion channels.

base.update_signal: platform changes how engagement counts are computed or displayed

pros.claim: Ratio disproportion is platform-agnostic and resistant to per-account obfuscation because it aggregates the whole reaction
pros.example: 100k likes with 4 comments signals purchased likes, not a real conversation

cons.claim: Baseline 'normal' ratios vary wildly by topic, format, and audience, so a fixed baseline mislabels organic outliers
cons.example: a meme legitimately gets huge likes and almost no comments

failure_modes: topic/format-dependent baselines mislabel organic outliers
platform reach-metric changes invalidate stored baselines
acceptance_tests: engagement ratios are compared to a topic/format-matched baseline and the baseline source is recorded
revisit_triggers: platform changes engagement metric definitions
an organic format produces a false disproportion flag

nodes.definition: Fuse the signal families (account, text, timing, network, engagement) into a single inauthenticity score via a documented weighting/model, keeping per-family contributions inspectable so the final score can be decomposed into its evidence sources.

base.update_signal: a signal family is added/removed or its reliability rating changes the fusion weights

excluded: calibration to a probability (handled by CALIBRATION)

pros.claim: Multi-signal fusion is far more robust than any single family, matching Botometer's ensemble-over-feature-classes design
pros.example: timing + network + text agreeing raises confidence beyond any one signal

cons.claim: Fusion can launder a weak, correlated set of signals into a falsely confident composite score
cons.example: five features that all derive from the same burst double-count one event

failure_modes: correlated signals double-count one underlying event
opaque weights make the score uninterpretable and unappealable
acceptance_tests: the fused score decomposes into per-family contributions that sum/trace back to logged signals
revisit_triggers: a signal family is added or removed
family reliability ratings are revised

nodes.definition: Map the raw fused score to a calibrated probability using Platt scaling (Platt 1999) or isotonic regression (Zadrozny & Elkan 2002) fit on the labeled validation set, and report the reliability diagram plus FPR/TPR at operating points so 0.7 means roughly 70% empirical inauthenticity.

base.update_signal: the validation label distribution shifts or the base rate of the deployment population changes

excluded: the no-data confirmation of ground truth

pros.claim: Calibration makes the probability semantically meaningful and comparable across reactions, per Niculescu-Mizil 2005
pros.example: after Platt scaling a 0.8 cohort is empirically ~80% inauthentic in validation

cons.claim: Calibration is only valid for populations matching the validation set; base-rate shift silently miscalibrates
cons.example: a model calibrated on bot-heavy data is overconfident on a clean feed

failure_modes: base-rate shift between validation and deployment breaks calibration
tiny or skewed validation sets yield unstable calibration curves
acceptance_tests: a reliability diagram is produced and the calibrated probability's empirical accuracy is reported with FPR/TPR
revisit_triggers: deployment base rate diverges from the validation set
the reliability diagram shows systematic miscalibration

nodes.definition: Attach an uncertainty interval to the point probability (e.g. via bootstrap over signals or Bayesian posterior) so a 0.6 estimated from sparse, noisy public signals is reported with a wide band, distinguishing 'confidently uncertain' from 'uncertainly confident'.

base.update_signal: the signal-sparsity regime or interval method changes

included: interval reporting alongside the point estimate

pros.claim: An interval prevents over-trusting a point estimate built on a handful of public signals
pros.example: P=0.6 [0.35,0.82] tells a reviewer not to act on the point alone

cons.claim: Intervals add cognitive load and are easy for consumers to ignore or misread
cons.example: a reviewer reads only the 0.6 and ignores the wide band

failure_modes: wide intervals are dropped by consumers who read only the point estimate
interval method understates uncertainty under correlated signals
acceptance_tests: each probability ships with an uncertainty interval whose width grows as signal sparsity grows
revisit_triggers: signal sparsity regime changes
consumers are observed ignoring the interval

nodes.definition: Build topic/format/audience-matched baselines of what organic timing, engagement ratios, and account mixes look like, so anomaly is measured as deviation from a like-for-like organic reference rather than against a single global norm that mislabels legitimate outliers.

base.update_signal: a platform format change or audience shift moves the organic reference distribution

pros.claim: Like-for-like organic baselines stop fixed global norms from flagging naturally skewed organic content
pros.example: a meme is compared to other memes, not to news-article engagement

cons.claim: Good organic baselines are themselves contaminated by undetected inauthenticity, biasing the reference
cons.example: the 'organic' baseline already contains unflagged bot activity

failure_modes: a contaminated baseline normalizes away real inauthenticity
too-narrow baselines have too little data to be stable
acceptance_tests: anomaly scores are computed as deviation from a topic/format-matched, versioned organic baseline
revisit_triggers: a platform format change shifts organic norms
a baseline is found to be contaminated by inauthentic activity

nodes.definition: Corroborate a suspected inauthentic reaction across platforms and surfaces: shared shortened URLs, identical media hashes, synchronized cross-site posting, and reused infrastructure, the linkage method Graphika and Meta use to attribute a single coordinated operation spanning multiple networks.

base.update_signal: a platform restricts cross-site signals or the operation changes its shared infrastructure

excluded: legal attribution to a named operator

pros.claim: Cross-platform linkage corroborates single-platform suspicion and is central to Graphika/Meta CIB attribution
pros.example: the same shortened URL seeded simultaneously across four networks reveals one operation

cons.claim: Cross-platform data is even sparser and harder to join reliably, raising both false links and missed links
cons.example: a coincidental URL reshare is mistaken for coordinated cross-posting

failure_modes: coincidental cross-site overlap mistaken for one operation
missing cross-platform data hides a multi-network campaign
acceptance_tests: cross-platform links are reported with the shared artifact (URL/hash/infrastructure) and a join-confidence recorded
revisit_triggers: a platform restricts cross-site signals
a coincidental overlap produces a false cross-platform link

nodes.definition: Curate and version a benchmark of labeled accounts/reactions from known CIB datasets (Cresci 2017 social-spambot corpora, Botometer's annotated sets, published Meta/Graphika takedown account lists) to measure detector FPR/TPR and to fit calibration, acknowledging label provenance and staleness.

base.update_signal: a new labeled CIB dataset is released or existing labels are revised/retracted

pros.claim: A versioned labeled benchmark is the only way to quote FPR/TPR honestly and to fit calibration, as Cresci 2017 enabled
pros.example: Cresci's social-spambot corpora became a standard CIB benchmark

cons.claim: Public CIB labels are stale and platform-specific, so benchmark performance overstates live accuracy
cons.example: 2017 spambots look nothing like 2024 LLM-driven accounts

failure_modes: stale labels make the benchmark unrepresentative of current adversaries
label leakage between train and test inflates reported accuracy
acceptance_tests: the benchmark is versioned with label sources, dates, and train/test splits documented to prevent leakage
revisit_triggers: a new CIB dataset is published
benchmark accuracy diverges from spot-checked live performance

nodes.definition: Model the adversarial arms race: bot operators evolve (LLM-generated text, jittered timing, aged accounts, residential proxies) so any fixed detector decays; track per-signal decay and schedule re-fitting, per Cresci 2017's 'paradigm shift' and Ferrara 2016's evolving-bots thesis.

base.update_signal: a new evasion technique is observed in the wild or a signal's TPR drops over time

pros.claim: Explicitly modeling decay prevents silent confidence in a detector the adversary already beat, the central lesson of Cresci 2017
pros.example: social spambots evaded all detectors that worked on the previous bot generation

cons.claim: Chasing every evasion technique causes overfitting to the last attack and detector instability
cons.example: retuning weekly to the newest trick degrades generalization

failure_modes: detector decays silently as adversaries adapt and no one notices
over-frequent re-fitting overfits to the most recent campaign
acceptance_tests: per-signal TPR is tracked over time and a re-fit is triggered when any signal's discriminative power decays below threshold
revisit_triggers: a novel evasion technique is reported
a signal's measured TPR drops over successive validation runs

nodes.definition: Encode the asymmetric harm of false positives: wrongly labeling a real user or community as inauthentic causes reputational, legal, and chilling-effect harm that usually outweighs missing some bots, so the decision policy is FP-averse and the cost asymmetry is explicit.

base.update_signal: the deployment context changes the relative cost of false positives vs false negatives

included: explicit FP vs FN cost weights

pros.claim: Making FP cost explicit forces conservative action on weak evidence and protects real users from defamation
pros.example: flagging an activist network as 'bots' on thin evidence causes real-world harm

cons.claim: Strong FP aversion lets genuine large coordinated campaigns pass under-actioned
cons.example: an FP-averse policy under-flags a real influence operation

failure_modes: uniform error cost mislabels real users at scale
over-aversion lets coordinated campaigns run unchallenged
acceptance_tests: the decision policy uses explicit, asymmetric FP/FN costs and documents the harm of each possible action
revisit_triggers: deployment stakes change the cost asymmetry
a false-positive incident harms a real user or community

nodes.definition: Define probability bands that route cases: low band auto-clears, high band with low uncertainty escalates, and the ambiguous middle (and any high-uncertainty case) routes to a human reviewer; no automated action is taken on a public-only probability without this gate when stakes are high.

base.update_signal: the action stakes, FP cost weights, or reviewer capacity change

pros.claim: A review band keeps a human accountable for high-stakes calls on probabilistic, public-only evidence
pros.example: P>0.85 with a tight interval escalates; 0.4-0.7 always gets human eyes

cons.claim: Review capacity is finite, so wide review bands create backlogs and pressure to widen auto-action
cons.example: a flood of ambiguous cases overwhelms the review queue

failure_modes: band boundaries set without cost grounding mis-route cases
review backlog pressures unsafe auto-actioning
acceptance_tests: routing bands are defined from FP/FN costs and uncertainty, and high-stakes actions require human review
revisit_triggers: reviewer capacity changes
FP cost weights are revised

nodes.definition: Propagate the calibrated authenticity probability downstream so that any hype/virality/trend metric computed over the reaction is discounted by its estimated inauthentic fraction, preventing inflated reach numbers from feeding decisions as if organic.

base.update_signal: a downstream consumer changes how it ingests the authenticity discount

included: propagation of the probability and its interval downstream
flagging of discounted vs raw metrics

pros.claim: Discounting hype by estimated inauthentic fraction stops manufactured virality from driving real decisions
pros.example: a trend with 60% likely-inauthentic amplification is downweighted before ranking

cons.claim: A wrong discount distorts genuinely organic trends as much as it corrects manufactured ones
cons.example: over-discounting buries a real grassroots surge

failure_modes: discount applied as a hard cut loses the uncertainty band
downstream consumers ignore the discount and use raw reach
acceptance_tests: downstream hype metrics carry the authenticity discount and its uncertainty, not a silently corrected number
revisit_triggers: a downstream consumer changes ingestion of the discount
over-discounting suppresses a verified organic trend

nodes.definition: Attach to every probability a human-readable provenance object: which signals fired, their weights, the matching examples (template cluster, burst window, ring members), the calibration version, and the validation FPR/TPR, so the estimate is auditable and appealable rather than an opaque number.

base.update_signal: the provenance schema or audit/appeal requirements change

included: contributing-signal list with weights and examples

pros.claim: Provenance turns a contestable number into an auditable claim, mirroring how Graphika reports show their evidence
pros.example: the report cites the 90-second burst window and the 12-word template as the evidence

cons.claim: Rich provenance can expose detection heuristics to adversaries who then engineer around them
cons.example: publishing exact thresholds teaches operators how to evade

failure_modes: provenance leaks heuristics that adversaries exploit
missing provenance makes an estimate impossible to appeal or audit
acceptance_tests: every probability carries a provenance object listing contributing signals, weights, examples, and calibration version
revisit_triggers: audit or appeal requirements change
a provenance leak is found to aid evasion

nodes.definition: Define and enforce the final output contract: a calibrated probability in [0,1], its uncertainty interval, the provenance object, the calibration/validation version, and an explicit 'no boolean verdict' invariant, so no consumer can extract a clean yes/no the data cannot support.

base.update_signal: a consumer requires a schema change, or governance mandates a different output form

pros.claim: A hard schema invariant is the only durable defense against the boolean collapse that public-only data cannot justify
pros.example: the schema has no 'is_bot' field, only a calibrated probability with provenance

cons.claim: A strict no-boolean contract frustrates simple integrations that genuinely need a gated action
cons.example: an automated mute rule still needs a threshold somewhere downstream

failure_modes: a consumer post-processes the probability into an unprovenanced boolean
schema drift reintroduces a verdict field
acceptance_tests: the output schema validates: probability + interval + provenance present, and no boolean verdict field exists
revisit_triggers: a consumer requests a boolean field
governance mandates a different output form

edges.why_related: observed signal decay feeds back to re-weight or retire fusion features
paraphrase/LLM evasion feeds back to update near-duplicate detection
benchmark labels are the data the calibration map is fit against
the absence of public ground truth constrains the output to a probability, not a verdict
FP-aversion constrains how aggressively authenticity discounts downstream hype
the provenance trail is the evidence a human reviewer adjudicates on
organic baselines define the deviation magnitudes the fusion model consumes as features
cross-platform linkage raises the corroborated inauthenticity contribution in fusion
the organic baseline grounds the inauthentic-fraction estimate used to discount hype

edges.resolution_rule: weight coordination evidence by FP cost: synchronized bursts alone never cross the action threshold for an authentic-looking organized community without corroborating network/text signals and human review
edges.why_related: aggressive coordination detection raises false positives against legitimate organized communities (fandoms, activism)
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: re-fit calibration on the freshest labeled slice whenever adversarial decay is detected; treat a calibration as valid only for the adversary generation it was fit on
edges.why_related: adversarial evolution invalidates a previously well-calibrated probability, so static calibration drifts out of date
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: discount hype by the calibrated inauthentic fraction with its interval, never by a raw ratio anomaly; a topic-baseline mismatch must not hard-cut an organic trend
edges.why_related: raw engagement disproportion can over-discount genuinely organic viral content with naturally skewed ratios
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: the model proposes; the human disposes on high-stakes cases: a high fused score never auto-actions when uncertainty is wide or FP cost is high, regardless of model confidence
edges.why_related: an automated high-confidence fused score conflicts with the requirement for human accountability on high-stakes public-only calls
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

conflict_axes.name: probability_vs_boolean_verdict
conflict_axes.description: Public-only signals support a calibrated probability but not a clean yes/no; consumers pressure for a boolean the data cannot justify.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: enforce a no-boolean output contract; push any thresholding downstream of the probability+provenance

conflict_axes.name: sensitivity_vs_false_positive_cost
conflict_axes.description: More aggressive detection catches more bots but mislabels more real users; FP harm is asymmetric.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight evidence by explicit asymmetric FP/FN cost and route ambiguous cases to humans

conflict_axes.name: authentic_coordination_vs_inauthentic_coordination
conflict_axes.description: Fandoms, activism, and breaking-news crowds coordinate organically and resemble CIB's synchronized timing.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require corroborating network/account signals before treating synchronized timing as inauthentic

conflict_axes.name: detector_stability_vs_adversarial_chase
conflict_axes.description: A fixed detector decays as adversaries adapt, but chasing every new evasion overfits to the last attack.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: track per-signal decay and re-fit only on measured TPR drops, not on every reported trick

conflict_axes.name: benchmark_fidelity_vs_label_staleness
conflict_axes.description: Labeled CIB benchmarks enable honest FPR/TPR but are stale and platform-specific, overstating live accuracy.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: version benchmarks with label dates; discount reported accuracy by staleness

conflict_axes.name: calibration_fit_vs_base_rate_shift
conflict_axes.description: Calibration is only valid for populations matching the validation set; deployment base-rate shift miscalibrates silently.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-estimate base rate at deployment and recalibrate or widen the interval

conflict_axes.name: signal_fusion_power_vs_correlated_double_counting
conflict_axes.description: Fusing signal families is robust but can double-count correlated signals derived from one underlying event.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decorrelate families and decompose the score so one event cannot be counted five times

conflict_axes.name: provenance_transparency_vs_evasion_exposure
conflict_axes.description: Rich provenance enables audit and appeal but can teach adversaries exactly how to evade.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: expose evidence categories and examples to reviewers; withhold exact thresholds from public output

conflict_axes.name: point_estimate_actionability_vs_uncertainty_honesty
conflict_axes.description: A point probability is easy to act on but hides the wide uncertainty intrinsic to sparse public signals.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always ship the interval with the point and gate actions on interval width

edge_cases.description: A real, organically coordinated community (a fandom mass-reply) is flagged as inauthentic coordination.
edge_cases.trigger: synchronized-timing detection fires on authentic organized activity with no corroboration
edge_cases.mitigation: require corroborating network/account signals and route to human review before action

edge_cases.description: A campaign uses LLM-paraphrased text so every post is unique, defeating near-duplicate detection.
edge_cases.trigger: template-spinning / model rewriting raises textual diversity above the similarity threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: track text-signal decay; lean on timing/network signals; re-fit detection

edge_cases.description: A public-only probability is collapsed into a boolean 'is_bot' flag by a downstream consumer.
edge_cases.trigger: a consumer thresholds the probability and drops the provenance and interval
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce the no-boolean output contract; require provenance to travel with any derived flag

edge_cases.description: Calibration fit on bot-heavy validation data is overconfident on a clean live feed (base-rate shift).
edge_cases.trigger: deployment base rate of inauthenticity diverges sharply from the validation set
edge_cases.mitigation: re-estimate deployment base rate and recalibrate or widen the uncertainty interval

edge_cases.description: Five fused signals all derive from one synchronized burst, so the score double-counts a single event.
edge_cases.trigger: correlated signal families are summed as if independent
edge_cases.mitigation: decorrelate families and cap the contribution of any single underlying event

edge_cases.description: Partial/sampled follower graph fabricates or hides a sybil ring.
edge_cases.trigger: API rate limits return only a fraction of the real edges
edge_cases.mitigation: record graph sampling coverage; downweight network signal when coverage is low

edge_cases.description: A new real user with a default avatar and empty bio is scored as a likely bot.
edge_cases.trigger: account-feature heuristics over-penalize legitimate new users
edge_cases.mitigation: use soft anomaly thresholds, never hard cutoffs; weight by FP cost

edge_cases.description: An organic meme with naturally skewed likes-to-comments ratio is flagged as purchased engagement.
edge_cases.trigger: a fixed engagement baseline ignores topic/format variation
edge_cases.mitigation: compare against topic/format-matched baselines; never hard-cut on ratio alone

edge_cases.description: Published provenance thresholds teach operators exactly how to stay under detection.
edge_cases.trigger: exact heuristic thresholds are exposed in public output
edge_cases.mitigation: expose evidence categories to reviewers; withhold exact thresholds publicly

edge_cases.description: A detector silently decays as the adversary evolves and confidence stays high while TPR collapses.
edge_cases.trigger: no per-signal decay tracking is in place
edge_cases.mitigation: track per-signal TPR over time; trigger re-fit on measured decay

edge_cases.description: A high fused score auto-actions on a high-stakes case despite a wide uncertainty interval.
edge_cases.trigger: the human-review gate is bypassed under queue pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: hard-gate high-stakes actions on interval width and FP cost; never auto-action wide-interval cases

edge_cases.description: Acknowledged public-data uncertainty is weaponized to dismiss a well-evidenced coordinated campaign.
edge_cases.trigger: adversary or stakeholder argues 'you can't prove it' against corroborated CIB evidence
edge_cases.mitigation: present the calibrated probability with full provenance and FPR/TPR, not a deniable single number

workflow.description: Fix the task as estimating P(inauthentic | public signals) for a visible reaction, with provenance and no boolean verdict.
workflow.gate: output target is a probability+provenance, not a boolean

workflow.description: Enumerate the private confirming signals that are unavailable and mark every estimate as proxied, not measured.
Collect public signals with provenance, freshness, and reliability per signal.
workflow.gate: every signal has a logged collection method and timestamp

workflow.description: Compute account-anomaly features and near-duplicate text clusters.
workflow.gate: features computed with soft thresholds, not hard cutoffs

workflow.description: Detect synchronized bursts, lockstep timing, and repeated co-action over logged windows.
workflow.gate: window parameters logged with each coordination score

workflow.description: Mine reciprocal clusters/sybil rings and score engagement-ratio disproportion.
Fuse signal families into a decomposable inauthenticity score traceable to logged signals.
Map the fused score to a calibrated probability via Platt/isotonic on the labeled benchmark; report FPR/TPR.
Attach an uncertainty interval that widens with signal sparsity.
Apply asymmetric FP/FN costs and route by probability/uncertainty band; gate high-stakes actions on human review.
Discount downstream hype by the inauthentic fraction and attach the provenance trail.
workflow.gate: hype metrics carry the discount and its interval

workflow.description: Emit the probability + interval + provenance + version stamps; validate the no-boolean invariant.
workflow.gate: schema validates and contains no boolean verdict field

dominance_rules.rule: PROBLEM_FRAMING and the no-boolean OUTPUT_CONTRACT must be fixed before any signal is scored for action
dominance_rules.rationale: a downstream boolean cannot be justified by public-only data; framing must precede scoring
dominance_rules.trigger: a scoring pipeline starts without the probability+provenance contract
dominance_rules.action: block until the output contract forbids a boolean verdict

dominance_rules.rule: NO_GROUND_TRUTH gap must be documented before any signal is treated as confirming inauthenticity
dominance_rules.rationale: public proxies are not internal labels; over-claiming creates legal and reputational risk
dominance_rules.trigger: a public proxy is asserted as confirmed ground truth
dominance_rules.action: require the unavailable confirming signals to be logged as proxied

dominance_rules.rule: CALIBRATION must be fit on a versioned VALIDATION_SET before any probability is reported
dominance_rules.rationale: an uncalibrated score is not a probability and FPR/TPR cannot be quoted honestly
dominance_rules.trigger: a raw score is shipped as if it were a probability
dominance_rules.action: block until a reliability diagram and FPR/TPR exist

dominance_rules.rule: FALSE_POSITIVE_COST weights must be set before HUMAN_REVIEW_THRESHOLD bands are drawn
dominance_rules.rationale: routing bands are derived from the asymmetric cost of false positives
dominance_rules.trigger: review bands set without explicit FP/FN costs
dominance_rules.action: require cost weights before band definition

dominance_rules.rule: High-stakes actions must pass HUMAN_REVIEW_THRESHOLD when uncertainty is wide or FP cost is high
dominance_rules.rationale: public-only probabilistic evidence requires human accountability on consequential calls
dominance_rules.trigger: an auto-action on a wide-interval high-stakes case
dominance_rules.action: hard-gate the action on human review

dominance_rules.rule: FEATURE_FUSION must decorrelate signal families before fusing
dominance_rules.rationale: correlated families derived from one event double-count and falsely inflate confidence
dominance_rules.action: decorrelate and cap any single event's contribution

dominance_rules.rule: ADVERSARIAL_ADAPTATION decay tracking must run before trusting a fixed detector over time
dominance_rules.rationale: detectors decay silently as adversaries evolve, per Cresci 2017
dominance_rules.trigger: a detector is trusted without per-signal TPR monitoring
dominance_rules.action: require per-signal decay tracking and re-fit triggers

dominance_rules.rule: EXPLANATION_PROVENANCE must accompany every reported probability
dominance_rules.rationale: an opaque number is unappealable and indistinguishable from a verdict
dominance_rules.trigger: a probability is emitted without an evidence trail
dominance_rules.action: block output until provenance is attached

dominance_rules.rule: CONFIDENCE_PROPAGATION discounts must carry the uncertainty interval, never a hard cut
dominance_rules.rationale: a hard discount distorts organic trends as much as it corrects manufactured ones
dominance_rules.trigger: a downstream metric is hard-cut by a point estimate
dominance_rules.action: require the interval to travel with the discount

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not score signals for action before fixing the probability+provenance output contract; retrofitting it after a boolean shipped is costly and harmful
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a defamatory hard 'bot' label that must later be retracted and re-engineered into a probability

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not treat a public proxy as confirmed ground truth; walking back an over-claim after publication is far costlier than hedging up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retraction of an over-claimed attribution and the trust damage it causes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not report a raw fused score as a probability; calibrating after the fact invalidates every prior reported number
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-issuing all previously reported probabilities once calibration reveals miscalibration

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not draw human-review bands before setting FP/FN costs; re-routing the entire case queue after a cost change is expensive
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-adjudication of a backlog routed under the wrong cost assumptions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not fuse correlated signal families as independent; unwinding double-counted confidence after action is costly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reversing actions taken on a falsely confident composite score

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy a detector without decay tracking; discovering silent decay after a missed campaign forces a full re-fit and post-mortem
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency re-fitting and incident review after an undetected evolved-bot campaign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not emit a probability without provenance; reconstructing the evidence trail during an appeal requires re-running the whole pipeline
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unappealable estimates that collapse under audit and force full re-computation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not hard-cut downstream hype by a point estimate; restoring a wrongly suppressed organic trend after the fact is costly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-instating a buried grassroots trend and recomputing affected rankings

iteration_protocol.trigger: a downstream consumer collapses the probability into a boolean verdict
iteration_protocol.action: re-assert the no-boolean OUTPUT_CONTRACT and require provenance to travel with any derived flag in PROBLEM_FRAMING

iteration_protocol.trigger: per-signal TPR decays or a novel evasion technique is observed
iteration_protocol.action: update the evasion catalog in ADVERSARIAL_ADAPTATION and re-fit FEATURE_FUSION and CALIBRATION on the freshest labeled slice

iteration_protocol.trigger: a false positive harms a real user or community
iteration_protocol.action: raise FP cost weights in FALSE_POSITIVE_COST and tighten the human-review band in HUMAN_REVIEW_THRESHOLD

iteration_protocol.trigger: deployment base rate diverges from the validation set
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate the base rate and recalibrate or widen the interval in CALIBRATION and UNCERTAINTY_QUANT

iteration_protocol.trigger: graph sampling coverage drops below a usable threshold
iteration_protocol.action: downweight the network signal in FEATURE_FUSION and record coverage in SIGNAL_INVENTORY

iteration_protocol.trigger: an authentic organized community is flagged as coordinated inauthentic behavior
iteration_protocol.action: require corroborating signals in COORDINATION_SIGNALS and route to human review in HUMAN_REVIEW_THRESHOLD

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new labeled CIB dataset is released
iteration_protocol.action: version it into VALIDATION_SET and re-measure FPR/TPR and recalibrate

priority_rationale: PROBLEM_FRAMING/NO_GROUND_TRUTH/SIGNAL_INVENTORY set the epistemic frame; the five signal families feed FEATURE_FUSION; CALIBRATION and UNCERTAINTY_QUANT make the score an honest probability; FALSE_POSITIVE_COST, HUMAN_REVIEW_THRESHOLD, provenance and the OUTPUT_CONTRACT enforce the probability-not-verdict finding last.
